title: Minimize Maximum Pair Sum in Array
statement:
`nums` has an even length `n`. Split all of its elements into `n / 2` pairs, using every element in exactly one pair. A pair's sum is its two elements added together, and the cost of a split is the largest pair sum it contains.

Return the smallest cost any split can achieve.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every way to pair the elements is hopeless: there are `(n-1)·(n-3)·…·1` pairings. Look at the largest element instead. It must sit in some pair, and the cheapest partner for it is the smallest element. Swapping partners to achieve this never raises the maximum, so after removing those two the same argument repeats on what is left. In sorted order this means pairing the outside elements and moving inwards.

## Approach

1. Sort a copy of `nums` into `sorted`.
2. Put `left` on the smallest value and `right` on the largest.
3. While `left < right`, add `sorted[left]` and `sorted[right]` into `pairSum` and keep the largest one in `best`.
4. Step both pointers inwards to form the next pair.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3,5,2,3]` sorts to `[2,3,3,5]`.

- `left = 0`, `right = 3`: `pairSum = 2 + 5 = 7`, `best = 7`.
- `left = 1`, `right = 2`: `pairSum = 3 + 3 = 6`, `best` stays `7`.

The pointers cross, so the answer is `7`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(n) for the sorted copy (O(1) extra if you sort in place).

## Pitfalls

- JavaScript's default `sort` compares strings; pass `(a, b) => a - b`.
- Pairing neighbours in sorted order (`sorted[0]` with `sorted[1]`) is wrong: it puts the two largest values together.
- You need the maximum over all pairs, not the sum of all pairs or the last pair formed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sorted` | the values in increasing order |
| `left`, `right` | the smallest and largest values not yet paired |
| `pairSum` | the sum of the current pair |
| `best` | the largest pair sum so far, which is the answer at the end |

narration.2: Sort a copy so the smallest and largest values sit at the two ends.
narration.3: left starts at the smallest value...
narration.5: best will hold the largest pair sum of this pairing.
narration.7: Keep pairing until the two pointers meet in the middle.
narration.8: Pair the smallest remaining value with the largest remaining one.
narration.9: The cost of the pairing is its largest pair sum, so keep the maximum.
narration.10: Move left to the next smallest value...
narration.13: Every element is paired; best is the smallest possible maximum pair sum.
